imported_summary_claim:
The source is a research heading rather than a well-formed question. For a finite rational Laguerre--Gaussian Cohn--Elkies candidate, the report proves an a posteriori global sign certificate: after exact square-factor removal, rational mesh values with lower margin mu, covering radius eta, and derivative bound M certify the compact interval when mu >= M eta, while an explicit leading-coefficient inequality certifies the infinite tail. Applying this to Q on [0,infinity) and -P on [T,infinity), with an outward-rounded objective, rigorously converts a numerical candidate into a sphere-packing density bound. A separate proposition proves that the highest active Laguerre index must be odd and its coefficient positive.

Candidate contribution (certification lemma; novelty confidence low): Candidate novelty: the exact square-factor plus mesh--derivative--tail packet is a finite, independently checkable certificate for the global half-line signs and objective of a rational polynomial--Gaussian Cohn--Elkies candidate.
